inspection.method: Every named PNG viewed through view_image, in the requested candidate order; only the two allowed rubrics and named images were inspected.

scoring_notes: Scores evaluate each default/1280 pair together, with 1280 functional defects carrying real weight. Overall is holistic rather than an arithmetic average.
All candidates remain visibly assembled interfaces rather than paintings by the reference artist. None earns fits_between_samples.
Larger type is preserved in every recommendation. No recommendation removes Tricks, stats, content, or controls.
Viewport-edge cropping is not treated as proof of inaccessible content. The boards may scroll; weak or absent visible scroll affordance is evaluated separately.
The eight-stat strip is not sufficiently exposed in these captures to certify all eight labels at 1280. I do not invent collisions in unseen stats or infer that they have been removed.

Hung artwork identity and placement, preview banner, and excluded combat room/actors/plates/rail/cards are not scored. Combat background is a neutral constant 5, excluded from the comparative judgment; combat scores concern only floating words and their treatment/placement.
Fading Strength tags in captured animation are not treated as permanent unreadability.

rest.worst_problem: On rest at 1600x900 and 1280x800, the left Blanket Fort still reads as outlined tartan panels with a smooth luminous arch rather than weighted, folded cloth.
observations: Four distinct objects and wide option rows establish a strong usable hierarchy; at default size all four actions register together.
At 1280 the Pack up and go on title is legible; the fourth row reaches the scroll viewport edge, which is not proof of inaccessible content.
The lower explanatory lines in Rest and Sharpen a Trick sit against the inner bottom gold rules; give those lines more padding instead of shrinking type.
The illustrated pillow, anvil, candle and cup give each option a concrete object, but glossy dark panels lack the painted material variation of the references.

event.worst_problem: On event at both sizes, the central story surface is still a large upright framed parchment rectangle, with too little visible lectern structure to make it a convincing object in the alcove.
observations: The candle attached at the upper-left parchment corner, red bookmark and softly feathered moonbeams make the strongest tangible event treatment.
Dark ink remains legible through the narrative and visible choices at both sizes.
At 1280 risk/reward text wraps cleanly into two lines; lower choices continue beyond the viewport, with little visible cue that the sheet can scroll.
The shafts retain dark wall colour better than hard pale wedges, though the room remains layered illustration rather than a unified painting.

gameover.worst_problem: On gameover-1280 the very large centre showcase and tall Final Tricks cartouches push the supporting record down without a clear visual cue that the side columns and stats continue by scrolling.
observations: The large central Trick has readable rules at 1280; the visible final-Trick names are clear and properly enclosed.
The centre card dominates the record more than necessary; its huge frame feels less balanced than the reference selection boards.
Final Tricks are recognisable separate objects, a substantial improvement over a ruled text table.
The right cartouche grid remains quite glossy and the broad purple side-panel surfaces are coarse rather than painted damask.
The eight-stat strip is offscreen in this view; its actual label fit cannot be verified.

shop.worst_problem: On shop-1280, the far-right Boomerang Bone card clips its rules inside its own description frame, including the opening line and bottom text.
observations: The mixed-case Keepsake names avoid the broken-word capitals seen elsewhere and are legible at 1280.
Bell jars and jars share a horizontal support but the thin gold ledge lacks convincing countertop depth and contact shadows.
Descriptions on lower hanging labels have weak ink-to-paper contrast, especially compared with the brighter event choices.
The lower content reaches the scroll viewport edge; that is not evidence of removal, but a scroll cue would make continuation explicit.

combat-floaters.worst_problem: On combat-floaters-1280, both sides' effects form one central descending stack between the figures, so Weak, Dexterity and Regen are not clearly attached to the Kid's head.
observations: Engraved serif capitals in black cartouches with curved gold rims are the closest floating-word language to the references.
No words collide with one another, and the tags avoid placing plain text directly across faces.
The stack still dominates the space between actors and its lower entries approach the enemy status area; position two separate groups beside the respective heads.

rest.worst_problem: On rest at both sizes, the enlarged left fort exposes rigid tartan geometry and a hard-edged window-light beam rather than folds, sag and lantern-lit cloth.
observations: The option text is well separated from its gold border; visible text does not collide with the right cost badges.
At 1280 a very narrow description column creates many short lines within exceptionally tall option rows.
The common gritty purple panel fill makes actions feel like repeated bordered UI containers even though each has an individual object.
The lower choices extend beyond the viewport without an obvious visible scroll control; no inference of inaccessibility is made.

event.worst_problem: On event at both sizes, the two window shafts are flat grey polygons ending in pale geometric floor quads at the lower sides of the board.
observations: Narrative and visible choice text remain readable, including the two-line outcomes at 1280.
The parchment has useful texture, but its rectangular framing and the hard light wedges pull the whole room toward composited web scenery.
The paper is not convincingly attached to a lectern or its own lamp.

gameover.worst_problem: On gameover-1280 the centre Dig Up a Fight card's first rules line runs into the ATTACK ribbon above it.
observations: The Final Tricks area is visibly a two-column ruled text table, unlike the carved or framed objects of the references.
At default size the centre caption and explanatory sentence below the showcased card also crowd one another.
The left The Search heading touches the panel's bottom frame at default size; this is an internal layout collision rather than merely a viewport crop.
Eight stats cannot be certified from the visible strip; the bottom crop does not establish that they are missing.

shop.worst_problem: On shop-1280 the Knotted Handkerchief name overruns the narrow lower-left nameplate, while the far-right Boomerang Bone rules clip inside the card.
observations: The warm curtain behind the cards is attractive and gives the shelf depth.
Jars sit on separate little gold plinths against flat textured panels rather than a shared lit counter.
Large capitals increase label pressure, and the unframed lower descriptions feel like a product grid rather than an illustrated shop.

combat-floaters.worst_problem: On combat-floaters at both sizes, bare bold condition words are laid directly across each figure's face and upper body without a tag or ribbon.
observations: The two separate groups identify which figure receives each set more clearly than a single merged central stack.
The text itself is readable, but its soft black outline and lack of material enclosure have little relation to the reference ornament language.

rest.worst_problem: On rest at both sizes, the right Sharpen a Trick row carries a huge blurred brown ornamental background that competes with its smaller crisp frame and text.
observations: Distinct row backgrounds attempt to differentiate the actions, but their inconsistent apparent scale weakens the system.
The left fort remains a largely flat outlined fabric construction despite slightly gentler light.
Visible option text has comfortable vertical space, though badge widths force narrow prose columns at 1280.
The lower options continue offscreen with little visible scrolling affordance.

event.worst_problem: On event at both sizes, the upper-right parchment lamp is a flat geometric gold symbol rather than a painted lamp casting believable light on the paper.
observations: Soft moonlight preserves the purple-black walls and is considerably more convincing than a sharp translucent wedge.
The heavy bright gold outer parchment frame has depth but feels extruded and too uniform beside the finer antique ornament.
Narrative and visible choices have clear dark ink, with no evident internal text collision.

gameover.worst_problem: On gameover-1280 the right Final Tricks plaques have very tight gaps between the cost medallion, long names and frame, particularly Put Yourself Back Together.
observations: Small gold framed plaques with clear wrapping make the best final-Trick inventory of this set; they read as objects and show more individually readable entries.
The centre card is large enough for its rules without consuming as much of the board as HELIODOR's.
The regular rectangular plaque frames are still mechanically uniform; the references use more sculpted cartouches and uneven antique highlights.
The eight-stat strip is not exposed enough to judge all labels, and the continuation lacks an explicit visible scroll cue.

shop.worst_problem: On shop-1280 the far-right Boomerang Bone card clips its rules inside its frame, and the lower-left Knotted Handkerchief name breaks within the word across three lines.
observations: The dark wooden counter below the glass vessels is the most convincing shared support in the set.
Pale rough-edged paper descriptions create clearer dark-ink contrast than AMETRINE's dim plaques.
The curtain has visible curved folds and warm highlights, although the bright drape competes somewhat with cards.
Counter, glass and paper form a useful material system, but label widths and card-rule allocation need repair.

combat-floaters.worst_problem: On combat-floaters-1280 the central cartouche stack crosses the Kid's torso at the top and the enemy name/status region at the bottom, obscuring the ownership of the effects.
observations: The serif capitals and gold-rimmed black tags are stylistically appropriate.
The larger leftward overlap is less well contained than HELIODOR's placement.
The tags need separate head-side lanes, rather than a single central staircase of effects.

rest.worst_problem: On rest at both sizes, the blanket wall and purple cushions in the left vignette remain rigid outlines with smooth fills instead of soft, weighted fabric.
observations: Subdued row-specific dark materials are more coherent than IOLITE's enlarged background ornament.
At 1280 the Pack up and go on control has a clear title and separate helper line.
Visible option copy has enough vertical room, but descriptions are squeezed into narrow columns by the side badges.
The large right rows continue below the viewport with no obvious drawn scroll handle; this is a discoverability issue, not evidence that actions are unavailable.

event.worst_problem: On event at both sizes, the gold light bar along the parchment's upper-left edge reads as a glowing UI strip rather than a recognisable lamp on a lectern.
observations: Soft window light and the dark wall texture preserve the room's mood.
The narrative is comfortably inset; dark ink and the risk/reward colour contrast read well at 1280.
The central sheet remains too front-facing and rectangular to be a fully convincing piece of furniture.
Lower choices may be scrolled, but the visible scene gives little indication of that continuation.

gameover.worst_problem: On gameover at both sizes, the right Final Tricks are plain rounded dark rectangles with thin gold double borders rather than engraved cards or cartouches.
observations: The central showcased Trick has readable rules and balanced scale.
The visible final-Trick names fit clearly, but the web-style boxes break the surrounding carved ornamental language.
The lower record continues beyond the captured viewport without an obvious scroll affordance; unseen stats cannot be certified.

shop.worst_problem: On shop-1280 the lower merchandise nameplates split words such as Pocketful and Liquorice across lines, while the description plaques beneath them are too dark for their black ink.
observations: The shelf is continuous but its repeated bright horizontal gold sections still read more as UI bars than a wooden countertop.
The upper-right Boomerang Bone card has the same internal rules clipping visible in the other candidates.
Warm curtain folds add material depth, but dark paper labels and arbitrary word breaks undermine the tangible-shop effect.

combat-floaters.worst_problem: On combat-floaters-1280 the broad flat purple Vulnerable ribbon reaches across the Kid's face, and all six ribbons merge into a central stack with unclear ownership.
observations: The serif text is clear, but polygon ribbon tails and uniform saturated fill look like vector banners rather than aged painted fabric.
The disconnected thin gold outlines visible above several ribbons make their construction look layered and unfinished.
The effect text needs separate groups beside heads and a more tactile tag surface.

winner_reason: HELIODOR offers the most coherent whole-game language: curved black-and-gold cartouches, restrained serif hierarchy, distinct action objects, softer alcove light and readable merchandise nameplates repeat across contexts. It is not the most accomplished in every object: IOLITE's final-Trick plaques and wooden shop support are better. HELIODOR nevertheless has fewer incompatible material metaphors than IOLITE's oversized row textures, AMETRINE's web-like rectangles and flat ribbons, or ONYX's plain floating text and ruled tables. This is a choice of the most salvageable unified visual system, not a claim of reference-level painting.

winner_fixes.fix: Increase the rules well and card height, or provide a clearly indicated internal scroll region, so the opening and final lines remain readable at the existing type size; preserve every Trick and its rules.

winner_fixes.region: Both sizes, between and beside the two heads
winner_fixes.fix: Place the Kid's three tags in one head-side lane and the enemy's three in another, with separation and an ownership cue; preserve the current serif size and gold cartouche treatment.

winner_fixes.region: Both sizes, left Blanket Fort vignette
winner_fixes.fix: Paint fabric sag, overlapping seams, irregular quilting, compressed cushions and occluded folds; make the lantern illuminate nearby cloth and cast contact shadows instead of filling a smooth arch.

winner_fixes.region: Both sizes, Final Tricks grid and centre showcase
winner_fixes.fix: Use sculpted plaques with content-driven height and generous inner padding; slightly rebalance the centre showcase's frame allocation without shrinking its text or removing any Trick.

winner_fixes.region: Both sizes, bottoms of the Rest and Sharpen a Trick rows
winner_fixes.fix: Increase the lower inset so explanatory baselines clear the gold rule; retain broad text columns and the distinct pillow/anvil/candle/cup objects.

winner_fixes.region: Both sizes, Keepsakes and Snacks counter
winner_fixes.fix: Give all glass vessels a visible wooden top plane, rear edge, warm light falloff and individual contact shadows so they stand on one real counter.
Lighten the paper locally and darken its ink enough to read descriptions; allocate full-word wrapping and adequate vertical space at the existing larger type.
Show a believable lectern lip and angled side or pedestal, and connect the existing candle's light to the paper so it reads as a physical story object.

winner_fixes.region: Both sizes, scrollable board edges above the fixed footer
winner_fixes.fix: Draw a clear ornamental scrollbar or continuation arrow with space above the footer; verify the full four choices, every Trick and all eight stats by scrolling, without interpreting these captures' viewport crops as inaccessible content.

grafts.idea: Adopt its compact framed Final Tricks plaques and readable long-name wrapping, retaining HELIODOR's larger type and adding more inset space around cost medallions.
Adopt the shared dark wooden shelf and the rough-edged light paper description tags; these better connect glass objects, support and written labels.
Adopt the restrained differentiated dark row grounds and the 1280 footer's clear title/helper-line arrangement, while keeping HELIODOR's broad option text columns.
Borrow only the clear two-group association with the respective figures; offset both groups beside their heads and retain HELIODOR's serif cartouches rather than ONYX's bare text.
